Nuveen CPACE Lending Fund IV secured more than $1 billion at first close, taking commitments across the four-fund series above $3 billion since 2023.

Institutional demand is rising as insurers seek long-duration, investment-grade private credit backed by real assets.

C-PACE programs now operate across 39 US states and Washington, D.C., widening the financing market for energy efficiency and climate resilience upgrades.

Nuveen Green Capital has secured more than $1 billion at the first close of its fourth C-PACE lending fund, expanding institutional capital available for sustainable commercial real estate.

The close brings total commitments across the Nuveen CPACE Lending Fund series to more than $3 billion since its launch in 2023.

Nuveen manages more than $1.4 trillion in assets globally. Its affiliate, Nuveen Green Capital, manages more than $6 billion and specializes in Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy financing.

The latest fundraising follows 73% year-over-year growth at Nuveen Green Capital. The firm attributed the increase to higher proprietary origination volumes across its vertically integrated investment and lending platform.

Private credit meets building decarbonization

C-PACE is a public-private financing mechanism administered at the state level. It gives commercial property owners and developers access to long-term private capital for eligible building improvements.

Projects can include upgrades that improve energy and water efficiency or strengthen properties against climate risks.

For institutional investors, the structure also offers exposure to long-duration, investment-grade assets. That combination has become increasingly relevant as insurers expand private fixed-income allocations.

“Investors have committed to this strategy across four vintages because the fundamentals remain steady throughout variable market cycles. NGC’s vertically integrated platform continues to deliver a scaled, proprietary flow of C-PACE assets originated with established sponsors, combining compelling economics with measurable impact,” said Alexandra Cooley, CEO and CIO of Nuveen Green Capital.

“The momentum behind this raise has been bolstered by our track record of strong origination volume, deployment, and consistent performance. Since 2015, NGC has originated more than $6 billion in C-PACE financings across securitizations. Fund IV strengthens our leadership position with increasing balance sheet capacity that institutional borrowers value.”

RELATED ARTICLE: Nuveen Green Capital, CDPQ Launch $600 Million Program for Sustainable Commercial Real Estate

Insurers deepen private fixed-income allocations

Institutional demand provides an important backdrop to the fundraise.

Nuveen’s 2026 EQuilibrium survey found that 46% of North American insurers plan to increase private fixed-income allocations over the next two years. Among those investors, 53% identified private asset-backed securities such as C-PACE as a key target.

“The continued growth in commitments from across four funds tells us that insurers aren’t just testing this asset class – they’re building meaningful, repeatable allocations to it,” said Joseph Pursley, Nuveen Head of Insurance, Americas.

“Life insurers in particular continue to prioritize longer duration, investment grade, asset-backed securities with attractive risk-adjusted returns, and NGC’s C-PACE strategy consistently delivers on that mandate while advancing climate resiliency at scale. The demand we’re seeing for Fund IV – including new insurance LPs – reinforces that this is becoming a durable, core allocation for insurance portfolios rather than a one-off commitment.”

For investors, that shift links two major portfolio priorities. Insurers need assets that can match long-duration liabilities, while real estate owners face growing capital requirements for building upgrades.

State policy expands the financing pipeline

C-PACE is now active across 39 states and the District of Columbia. Continued legislative adoption could further expand the addressable market for lenders and institutional investors.

That policy structure is central to the asset class. State and local frameworks establish the mechanisms that allow private capital to finance eligible property improvements.

Nuveen Green Capital’s transactions already range from roughly $5 million to several hundred million dollars.

In 2025, the platform financed The Geneva, an office-to-residential conversion in Washington, D.C. The transaction became the largest C-PACE financing completed to date.

For property owners, access to larger pools of institutional capital could help fund retrofits and conversions at a time of higher borrowing costs and tighter traditional lending conditions.

For investors, Fund IV shows how climate-related real estate financing is moving deeper into private credit portfolios. As more US jurisdictions adopt C-PACE frameworks, the model could channel significantly more institutional capital into building efficiency and resilience while creating a larger investable market around the transition of existing real estate.
